newsitem.title: UK: UK's Hermes outlines corporate governance policies.
newsitem.headline: UK's Hermes outlines corporate governance policies.

text.p: Fund manager Hermes Investment Management on Monday joined the debate on corporate governance in the UK, stressing non-executive director independence and accountability.
It said it was writing to all the companies in which it invests setting out a revised policy on corporate governance and voting policies.
It suggested half of non-executive directors' (NED) pay should be in the form of shares, and that there be a minimum of three fully independent NEDs in a board.
Hermes is the executive arm of the British Telecommunications Plc Pension Scheme and invests 16 billion stg in UK equities. It has investments in all the companies in the FTSE All Share Index.
It said it would generally support incumbent management in a hostile takeover situation, but that this support was not unconditional.

Little change was currently required to the current, still new, corporate governance regimes, it said, and future changes should be introduced by refinement of best practice guidelines rather than legislation.

Hermes also said it did not consider executive directors who became NEDs without a break in service as independent, and similarly was opposed in principle to chief executives becoming chairmen without a break in service.
It stressed that shareholders should ensure NEDs are held accountable for their board responsibilities.
Hermes said the code was standard policy, but it would adopt a pragmatic approach when justified by circumstances.
"Management of companies run in the long term interests of shareholders can be confident of Hermes' continuing support," it said.
